proposal.utterance: How would you BFO-classify 'the capacity of an institution to repair itself'?

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity
entities.rationale: A capacity is paradigmatically a BFO Disposition: it is internally grounded in the bearer (the institution), it may or may not be realized, and it is triggered by circumstances calling for self-repair. BFO_0000016 (Disposition) is defined as a realizable entity that is grounded in the physical or social makeup of the bearer and is not merely an externally assigned role. 'The capacity to repair itself' fits this profile: it inheres in the institution by virtue of its internal structural and procedural properties (e.g., amendment procedures, review mechanisms), not merely by external assignment. This distinguishes it from a Role (BFO_0000023), which is externally grounded. It is also distinct from a Quality (BFO_0000019) because it is not a static measurable property but a directed potentiality toward a process of repair.

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess
entities.rationale: The realization of the self-repair capacity is a Process (BFO_0000015): a temporal unfolding in which the institution enacts corrective changes to its norms, structures, or practices. This class is proposed as the canonical realization target of InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity via BFO_0000054 (realized in). Without this class the disposition would have no typed realization target in the graph.

relations.rationale: Asserts InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity as a sub-kind of Disposition in the BFO hierarchy.
Asserts InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess as a sub-kind of Process in the BFO hierarchy.
A disposition is realized in a process; the capacity for institutional self-repair is realized in an actual self-repair process when triggered.

Self-repair capacity can be treated as a species of LegalExistenceCondition (already typed as BFO_0000016): the ability to reform itself is plausibly a condition for the ongoing legal existence of an institution. This is an open proposal subject to user confirmation.
Institutions (LegalInstitution, a material entity) are the bearers of this disposition; the relation bearer-of connects them.

open_questions: Should InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity be typed as a subclass of the existing LegalExistenceCondition (BFO_0000016), or kept as a direct subclass of BFO_0000016 without that further specialization?
Is the intended bearer exclusively a LegalInstitution, or should the capacity range over any social institution (broader than legal)?

Is 'self-repair' meant to cover only procedurally authorized reform (e.g., constitutional amendment) or also informal adaptive change? This affects whether one or multiple subclasses of InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess are needed.
Should InstitutionalEffectiveness (already in the graph as BFO_0000019 Quality) be linked to InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity as a quality that tracks the degree to which the capacity is actualized?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'the capacity of an institution to repair itself' most naturally maps to BFO_0000016 (Disposition), because a capacity is a realizable entity that is internally grounded in the bearer and directed toward a specific kind of process when triggered. Unlike a Quality (BFO_0000019), which is a static measurable property, and unlike a Role (BFO_0000023), which is externally conferred, a capacity-for-repair is grounded in the institution's own structural and procedural makeup — e.g., its amendment mechanisms, review bodies, or revision procedures. Two classes are proposed: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity (Disposition) as the capacity itself, and InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess (Process) as its canonical realization target, connected via BFO_0000054 (realized in). The existing class LegalInstitution (BFO_0000040) is the bearer via RO_0000053. A tentative subsumption link to LegalExistenceCondition is flagged as an open question because plausible but not entailed by the user's utterance alone.
